chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā al-Kāhilī, from Zurārah, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: I fast, and I do not take the midday rest until the sun passes the meridian. Then when the sun passes the meridian, I perform my nawāfil, then I perform ẓuhr, then I perform my nawāfil, then I perform ʿaṣr, then I sleep; and that is before the people perform salat. So he said: “O Zurārah, when the sun passes the meridian, the time has entered, but I dislike for you to make it a fixed habitual time.”

If it is said: you have mentioned that when the sun passes the meridian, the time of the obligatory salat has entered; then you said that beginning with the nawāfil is more virtuous, and this conflicts with what has been narrated in the reports that there is no supererogatory prayer during the time of an obligatory prayer.
(982) 19. Al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn Samāʿah narrated that from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

“A man from the people of al-Madīnah said to me: O Abā Jaʿfar, why is it that I do not see you performing supererogatory prayer between the adhān and the iqāmah as the people do?” He said: “I said: when we wish to perform supererogatory prayer, our supererogatory prayer is at a time other than the time of an obligatory prayer; so when the obligatory prayer enters, then there is no supererogatory prayer.”

key_terms.النَّوَافِلِ: supererogatory prayers performed in addition to the obligatory prayers
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةِ: the commencement call immediately before congregational salat
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: the sun passed the meridian; the onset of the noon prayer time

ai.seo_question: Can nawāfil be performed after the time of the obligatory noon prayer begins?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the timing of obligatory and supererogatory salat after the sun passes the meridian. It indicates that the time of the obligatory prayer begins at zawāl, while also addressing the preference and limits regarding nawāfil in relation to the entry of the obligatory prayer time. A supporting report from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that when the obligatory prayer time enters, no supererogatory prayer is performed.
